pointers.sentence: *What `login` writes into the session (`django/contrib/auth/__init__.py`).*

The primary key is written by the key field's `value_to_string` and read back by `_get_user_session_key` through the field's `to_python`: the comment there says the value in the session is always a string and has to be converted whenever it is read (`django/contrib/auth/__init__.py:_get_user_session_key`).
The backend's path is kept, in the documentation's words, so that the same backend can fetch the user on a later request (`docs/topics/auth/default.txt`).
`login(request, user, backend=None)` works in this order (`django/contrib/auth/__init__.py:login`):
The documentation gives the reason: it mitigates session fixation (`docs/topics/http/sessions.txt`).

`_set_auth_user` puts the user on the request: `HttpRequest.user` becomes the user itself in place of the lazy object, and `HttpRequest.auser` a coroutine function that returns it, each only if the request already had one (`django/contrib/auth/__init__.py:_set_auth_user`).

Django connects one receiver to `user_logged_in`, `update_last_login`, which sets `AbstractBaseUser.last_login` to the current time and saves that field alone (`django/contrib/auth/models.py:update_last_login`).

`AuthConfig.ready` connects it only when the user model's `last_login` is a field, a `DeferredAttribute` on the class; a custom user model that sets it to `None` gets no receiver (`django/contrib/auth/apps.py:AuthConfig.ready`).
`alogin` takes the same steps through the session's asynchronous methods and sends the signal with `Signal.asend` (`django/contrib/auth/__init__.py:alogin`).
`login` and `alogin` no longer fall back to the request's user when given `None` for the user (`docs/releases/6.1.txt`).
Then it flushes the session and puts an `AnonymousUser` on the request with `_set_auth_user` (`django/contrib/auth/__init__.py:logout`).

The documentation's reason for emptying the whole session: another person using the same browser should not reach the previous user's session data, and whatever is meant to outlast the logout is to be written after it (`docs/topics/auth/default.txt`).
`alogout` asks `HttpRequest.auser` for the user and flushes with `SessionBase.aflush` (`django/contrib/auth/__init__.py:alogout`).
Then it puts two things on the request and looks nothing up (`django/contrib/auth/middleware.py:AuthenticationMiddleware.process_request`).

`HttpRequest.user` is a `SimpleLazyObject` over the middleware module's `get_user`, which calls `django.contrib.auth.get_user` once and keeps the answer on the request as `"_cached_user"` (`django/contrib/auth/middleware.py:get_user`).

`HttpRequest.auser` is the module's coroutine function `auser`, bound to the request, which awaits `aget_user` once and keeps the answer as `"_acached_user"`, a cache of its own (`django/contrib/auth/middleware.py:auser`).

`aget_user` takes the steps of `django.contrib.auth.get_user` through `SessionBase.aget`, `SessionBase.acycle_key` and `SessionBase.aflush`, and asks the backend's `aget_user`, which `BaseBackend.aget_user` runs through `sync_to_async` and `ModelBackend.aget_user` answers with an asynchronous query (`django/contrib/auth/__init__.py:aget_user`).
`django.contrib.auth.get_user` takes these steps, and answers with an `AnonymousUser` wherever one fails (`django/contrib/auth/__init__.py:get_user`):

`AbstractBaseUser.get_session_auth_hash` is `salted_hmac` of the field `AbstractBaseUser.password`, the string the hasher stored and not the password, with the salt `"django.contrib.auth.models.AbstractBaseUser.get_session_auth_hash"`, the secret key and SHA-256, in hex (`django/contrib/auth/base_user.py:AbstractBaseUser._get_session_auth_hash`).
The documentation names the purpose: a user can log out every session by changing the password (`docs/topics/auth/default.txt`).

It cycles the session key, and writes the new hash when the user is the request's user (`django/contrib/auth/__init__.py:update_session_auth_hash`); the documentation's reason for the new key is that a stolen session cookie stops working (`docs/topics/auth/default.txt`).
